newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Monday due to short-covering with some investors moving their money to other active markets, traders said.
The key November 1996 contract ended at 3,305 yuan ($398) per tonne, unchanged from last Friday's close. It opened at an intra-day low of 3,262 and hit a high of 3,320.
January rose 20 to 3,205, March 29 to 3,239, May fell 10 to 3,380, July unchanged at 3,380 and September put on 20 to 3,400.
Combined volume rose to 19,100 tonnes from 9,900.
